  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

answer.rationale: The two measured declines are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), which are causally linked: onboarding completion is upstream of activation, so fixing friction there plausibly recovers both, while activation messaging only addresses the downstream symptom. Onboarding simplification is also the best-corroborated direction in inherited memory, supported independently by memory_31 (fewer required signup fields lifted SMB first-week activation, durable) and memory_86 (shorter onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value across self-serve). I am deliberately not choosing promotional_pricing even though it is the most direct answer to the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 records strong acquisition and revenue lift but a material 30-day retention drop and carries an explicit instruction not to generalize it as a growth strategy. Under a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, buying price-sensitive accounts that churn in 30 days converts the one non-recurring experiment slot into a revenue-quality loss. Referral_incentive (memory_57) is sound but targets established customers and does nothing for the two declining funnel metrics; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) addresses a segment that is not where the loss is occurring. Verification targets: memory_86 because it is the load-bearing claim for my chosen action and I need the original record to check whether the lift was in completion rate alone or in downstream qualified conversion, and whether it held for the same self-serve cohort now declining; memory_91 because it is the strongest alternative use of the slot and I want to know the effect size on activation before discarding it — if activation messaging shows a large, durable activation lift and memory_86's effect turns out to be completion-only vanity movement, I will switch. Downstream value risk: cutting required signup fields reduces the qualification data that the demo-request/sales-assisted enterprise path depends on (memory_44), so simplification must be scoped to the self-serve SMB path and must not strip fields used for enterprise routing; I am also aware that all six memories are consolidated summaries with archived sources, so effect sizes and durability windows are uncertain until pulled. Scale is a standard experiment with a retention and qualified-revenue guardrail, not a broad rollout, because none of these memories were measured under current competitive pressure.
